speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As I looked into the problem further, I found video after video of people diving in the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) waters full of plastic trash.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The plastic does not just stay in the sea.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It breaks down, releasing greenhouse gases that worsen global warming.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It chokes and kills a million seabirds and 100,000 marine mammals every year.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: And ultimately, it breaks down into microplastics and is eaten by fish, crabs and mussels.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This comes back to us on our plates, in our food.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It comes back a full circle and our own plastic trash harms us directly.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Plastic can no longer be seen just as an environmental problem.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It is also a danger to our own health.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It must be addressed as an urgent public safety issue.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Speaking at the Group of Seven (G7) Summit earlier this year, the United Nations (UN) Secretary General told world leaders that we are facing a "global emergency" over the plastic in our oceans, and that "leadership is needed now, more than ever" to protect "our collective future and security".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Thus, I am heartened to see that Singapore is taking the initiative in organising international cooperation on this issue, through the 13th East Asia Summit.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This November, Singapore will host officials from ASEAN countries along with several non-ASEAN countries, to discuss several issues, including a Statement on a Regional Plan of Action on Combatting Marine Plastic Debris.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Indonesia has pledged US$1 billion per year to various initiatives targeting plastic consumption and pollution.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Malaysia has just announced their zero-waste plan that aims to abolish single-use plastic by 2030.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The whole country or some cities in the United States, India, Myanmar, Australia, South Korea, Cambodia and China have either implemented some form of plastic bag charge or banned plastic bags or other single-use plastic items.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Soon, Brunei and New Zealand will join them.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Given that much of the world’s ocean plastic originates from here, in this region, our actions can have a truly global impact.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Singapore's platform as a regional leader and host of the East Asia Summit gives us the ability and responsibility to step up our own plastic reduction efforts at home and call on every member nation to do the same.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We are doing well at tackling the symptoms of the problem.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Singapore’s efficient waste management system ensures that litter in our waterways is removed with litter traps before it reaches the sea.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Whether the marine litter comes from us here in Singapore or other countries, it still ends up in our food and still washes up on Singapore's shores.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Just two weeks ago, Jo Teo shared on Facebook about her experience at an International Coastal Cleanup organised by Little Green Men: "Today was an eye-opening experience for me.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Having done beach cleanups with students, I’ve always thought that our beaches were ok.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Not too dirty, maybe an odd piece of litter here and there.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Perhaps we’ve always gone to 'cleaned' stretches of beaches." "Today, we were at a small stretch of Chek Jawa that is a little away from the boardwalk area where people typically visit.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: At first glance, it seemed to be fairly clean, yet in less than two hours, 30 plus of us collected well over 200 kilos of plastic!

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We were only cleaning a tiny stretch of coastline perhaps just 50 metres long!

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: What about those still in the water?” We can continue cleaning our shores and continue trapping litter before it enters our waters.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But we need to move beyond addressing symptoms of the problem.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In August, at the Foreign Ministers' meeting in advance of the East Asia Summit, the Ministers noted that one of the root causes of marine plastic debris is the excessive use of plastic bags.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: That is the root of the problem, which we must tackle in order to successfully combat marine plastic debris.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If every country just focuses on trapping waste before it enters the waters, we will be combating marine plastic debris problem forever.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We need to tackle the excessive use of plastic and I hope that Singapore will take the lead in this.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Even when I bring my own reusable bag to the supermarket, the cashier sometimes puts my groceries first into a plastic bag, and then into my reusable bag.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We really need to start thinking about our plastic bag use.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Senior Minister of State Amy Khor previously said, "Unlike many of the countries that have imposed a ban or mandatory plastic charge, plastic bag charge, we do not directly landfill our plastic disposables but incinerate them.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As such, we do not face the land and water pollution issues that plague those countries." But, Sir, is it okay to waste so much plastic, simply because our waste will be burned or removed from sewage discharge into the ocean?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Or phrased differently, is it alright to litter just because someone else will clean up after us?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Burning the excessive number of plastic bags we throw away is again addressing the symptoms of the problem.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Again, we need to tackle the root of the problem.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As Senior Minister of State Amy Khor has stated, we must "adopt a holistic approach and tackle this upstream".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We should go to the source of the problem and cut plastic waste by cutting plastic use.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Minister Masagos has also recently pointed this out, "the issue with plastic waste here   not about improper disposal, but about reducing the demand", and "everyone   together instead of waiting for someone else to take action".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: There are lots of people taking action in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This groundswell has also rippled through the private sector.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Multinational brands like Hyatt Hotels, Kentucky Fried Chicken (KFC) and IKEA, as well as local businesses like Unpackt, The Green Collective, Plain Vanilla, and Muthu's Curry, have taken the initiative to reduce or eliminate plastics in their operations.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: And just last month, the Development Bank of Singapore (DBS) launched "#recycle more, waste less", a nationwide campaign to discourage the use of single-use plastics.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In the public sector, the Government is engaging stakeholders to voluntarily reduce all types of packaging waste and cut the use of single-use plastic items.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We also have the Singapore Packaging Agreement, which encourages businesses to minimise packaging waste.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: At our new hawker centres, we have also disallowed the use of disposables for dine-ins.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: And lastly, the Ministry of the Environment and Water Resources (MEWR) will be developing an inaugural Zero Waste Masterplan to be released next year.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But the Government can and should do more.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In our Public Sector Sustainability Plan 2017 to 2020, the word "plastic" is only mentioned once, in the paragraph on recycling.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But I hope we can add the word "plastic waste reduction" to be more specific.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I hope we can put a stronger emphasis on the reduction component rather than the recycling.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Otherwise, we are again focusing on the symptoms of the problem.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The Senior Minister of State had previously stated that we ought to consider encouraging all Ministries and agencies to eliminate single-use plastics from their catering and events.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This is really what our Government ought to do in order to walk the talk and lead by example.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: And I hope we start this practice at Singapore's biggest party, our National Day Parade (NDP).

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This year's NDP fun pack contained many plastic items individually wrapped in plastic, and even an NDP 2018 plastic bag for each person to bag their waste.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If NDP 2019 next year were to use only reusable items with minimal packaging, it would send a strong signal that our nation is committed to building a sustainable world.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As Senior Minister of State Amy Khor had recently pointed out, substituting plastic bags with paper or other biodegradable plastic bags may have negative environmental outcomes, as the latter have higher carbon footprints.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I agree with the Senior Minister of State that we should ensure consumers do not substitute carrier bags but, instead, make the switch to bringing their own reusable bags.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Using one reusable bag a year can save 125 plastic bags from being littered or incinerated and the reduced demand for plastic would drastically decrease plastic production.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This Motion is about a plastic-lite Singapore, not a plastic-free Singapore.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: And I do understand the public concern that plastic bags are necessary to bag household trash.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I, too, use plastic bags to throw my rubbish down the rubbish chute.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: To make sure that the plastic bag charge policy is tailored to Singapore's unique situation, bags used to carry fresh produce should be exempted from this charge.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Using reusable bags to carry fresh produce, raw meat or seafood may be unhygienic, so plastic bags should be given out for free for such items.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I understand that Hong Kong is already doing this.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In this way, people can still obtain some free bags to bin their trash, maintaining the cleanliness and safety of our rubbish chutes and waste disposal system.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: There are, of course, critiques of what Hong Kong is doing, how people are gaming the system because of this free bag exemption, how enforcement is difficult – and if I may add, the media asked me about this yesterday – and how the compliant rate is only about 50%.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But, at least, Hong Kong is trying and I rather be optimistic and say, "Not bad, 50% of retailers are compliant; good start!" A plastic bag charge has proven to be effective in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As IKEA Singapore demonstrated, this charge can also be a stepping stone to comprehensively eliminate use of all disposable plastic items.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Today, they are working to remove all single-use plastic products from the IKEA range and restaurants by 2020.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Based on the survey by zero-waste Singapore, many Singaporeans have responded positively to the possibility of a plastic bag charge.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This may benefit retailers as well as customers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: When we receive plastic bags from shops, we often think we are getting them for free.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But, in fact, carrier bags may be a significant cost to retailers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: These costs are obviously passed on to consumers, raising product prices.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Hence, we are already paying for these plastic bags.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: A shift towards a plastic-lite practice throughout the retail industry will give customers more choice in whether to pay for plastic bags and also help retailers save money and the environment.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As such, while a plastic bag charge looks like it will increase cost for everyone, in fact, it will do the opposite and might help to bring cost down for everyone.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Although we live on this planet as if we had another one to go to, we do just have this planet we call home and we all need to save it, together and urgently.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: On the boat ride there, Ella exclaimed, "Look daddy, there is so much rubbish in the sea, we need to pick them up to save the animals".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It was shocking and painful to see so many plastic bags and bottles in the oceans, in Singapore waters.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I shared this on Facebook on Saturday night and you can see over 80 plastic bottles in the oceans in one of the photos I took.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: A four-year-old knows that we must do something to combat this plastic problem.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Surely, we, as the Government, should take the lead and do more.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But I hope the Senior Minister of State's reply to my speech will not focus on what we have done and what we are currently doing.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I hope her speech will focus on what more we can do, beyond incinerating the plastic, recycling plastic waste, trapping the waste before it enters our waters, the packaging agreement and the mandatory reporting.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Lastly, Sir, I hope the Senior Minister of State can address these questions.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I am sure she is going to find lots of plastic on our shores.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I sincerely hope that when my two other daughters Katie and Poppy grow up, there will no longer be a need to do coastal clean-ups.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: My Ministry believes the long-term approach is to engage Singaporeans on the importance of sustainability.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Quick fixes address the symptoms but not the root of the problem.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Hence, our aim is to build a national consciousness to care for the environment so that Singaporeans and businesses will take action, even beyond what the regulations require.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: This process may take longer, but that is the right way; the positive effects will go beyond plastic bags, beyond packaging, beyond waste management to areas, including climate action.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We see growing numbers of businesses and Singaporeans who go the extra mile to care for the environment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Mr Louis Ng himself is one such example.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: He has also cited many other examples and I notice that many of them are in the House today.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: This goes beyond plastic bags to include packaging, such as bottles and containers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Even as we seek to reduce plastic usage, we recognise that plastics have their uses; substituting them with other materials may not be more environmentally friendly, as some may perceive.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: For example, the British Government estimated that a cotton tote bag must be used 173 times before its greenhouse gas emission impact improves beyond the plastic bags we use to line our bins.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Our lifecycle assessment of common carrier bags had the same conclusion.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Hence, our approach is to reduce excessive consumption of all types of packaging, including plastics used by businesses and individuals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: This will focus management’s attention on the amount of packaging used and raise awareness of the potential to reduce packaging.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We are also studying the feasibility of adopting the Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) approach for packaging waste.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: This will impose collection targets on businesses who use or produce packaging.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: It incentivises businesses to reduce their packaging upstream and ensures the proper recycling of packaging downstream.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We will publish the details of these initiatives to address packaging waste, and other measures for e-waste, food waste and so forth in the inaugural Zero Waste Masterplan to be launched next year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We will not hesitate to legislate where necessary.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: But we will do so by taking a pragmatic and considered approach that suits our local context.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: While we will always seek to learn from others, it is never our practice in policymaking to simply follow what other countries have done.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Our efforts to address plastic waste go beyond our borders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We take the issue of marine plastic pollution seriously.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Singapore participates actively in regional and international discussions to address marine litter and microplastics.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: For example, under the Singapore-Norway Third Country Training Programme, the National Environment Agency (NEA) partnered experts from the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) and our Norwegian counterparts to share our expertise on waste management and pollution control, as well as the management of plastic waste and microplastics.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We are heartened by the efforts of various countries to tackle marine plastic pollution, as highlighted by Mr Louis Ng.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We have strict anti-littering measures and dispose of most general waste at our waste-to-energy plants to prevent marine pollution from land-based sources.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Any litter that enters our waterways is removed using litter traps and flotsam removal craft before it reaches the sea.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Marine pollution is caused by the improper disposal of plastic waste, and not the use of plastics per se.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: A 3 March Economist article entitled "The known unknowns of plastic pollution" reached the same conclusion.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Hence, our measures deal with the root cause of marine pollution and are not merely addressing symptoms, as Mr Louis Ng posited.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: That notwithstanding, we will continue to address the issue of marine plastics pollution through our stringent anti-littering measures, educating the public against littering and excessive consumption of plastics and introducing regulatory measures to minimise plastic and packaging waste upstream.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The public sector is also doing its part to promote green practices among its agencies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We have published a Best Practice Guide to guide agencies to organise environmentally friendly events.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: For example, we avoid the use of plastic bottled water and disposables by providing water dispensers and reusable crockery and cutlery where possible.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We will also continue to improve our Public Sector Sustainability Plan, where waste reduction is a key thrust, and I will try to make sure that "plastics" is mentioned more than once.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Under the plan, we require large buildings to report the amount of waste disposed and will set waste reduction targets for the public sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We do not serve bottled water for meetings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Our staff bring their own plates and cutlery for events to avoid the use of disposables.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We are encouraging other public sector agencies to do the same for their meetings and events, such as the NDP as well as community activities, to minimise the use of plastics.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Beyond what the public sector is doing, I am encouraged that many passionate groups and individuals like Plastic-Lite SG, UnPackt and Tabao Girl are moving the ground in their own ways.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Companies, such as KFC and IKEA, have similarly done so.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: NEA will support them if required, such as through the 3P Partnership Fund.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: This shows how we can multiply our impact if we all work in partnership.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: On the proposed carrier bag charge, we will continue to monitor developments in this area.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Mr Louis Ng referred to the Hong Kong system of giving free bags for hygiene purposes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: This addresses the issue of providing some bags to households for bagging their waste.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: An equal proportion of respondents ranked a plastic bag charge as their most and their least preferred option.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: There is still more we can do to persuade consumers not to take more than they need, and to bring their own reusable bags.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: As the same Economist article puts it, even though plastics is not at the top of environmental ills, it is highly visible, and I would say, emotional.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: This gives us the opening to encourage Singaporeans to form the right habits.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: I believe this is one area where we can work with our 3P partners to engage and educate Singaporeans and change their habits.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Let us give the policies that we have and will be putting in place time to take effect and for people to change habits.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I think the Senior Minister of State mentioned about encouraging, but can I confirm whether the Public Service is planning to eliminate single use plastic in our catering of events?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Same for NDP, I think the Senior Minister of State mentioned that we are going to encourage, but I think planning would have probably started for 2019.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: So, can I confirm that NDP 2019 will only use reusable items with minimal packaging?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Lastly, for the proposed carrier bag charge, can I ask whether MEWR can at least do a study on this issue and whether they can report back to this House once the study is completed?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, we have encouraged them to reduce the use of plastic bottles, plastic bags, as much as possible, as well as reduce packaging of their collaterals.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And what we can say is that we will encourage them to do this as much as possible because, for some events, including NDP and major events, it may not be possible to entirely do away with bottled water, and just use water dispensers, because of the large number of people.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, as far as practicable and applicable, we will encourage them to do so.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: With regard to NDP 2019, we will encourage the NDP organisers to do this also as much as it is practicable.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, what you really want to do is to go upstream.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And I suppose I will be disappointing the Member by reiterating and repeating what I have said in this House before and what I will be saying again on the same issues that the Member has also raised in this House that, really, what we want to do is move upstream.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As far as carrier bags are concerned, we think that it is more practicable, more sustainable, to take the long-term approach.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: It may take a longer time, but it is really to change habits, educate and encourage the public to reduce the use of disposables and all types of packaging.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Mr Louis Ng, you have only two more minutes.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I know we have the guidelines; I know this will not happen overnight as well.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Malaysia has announced that they are going to do it by 2030.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: So, I am just wondering if MEWR has a long-term plan of eliminating single-use plastics in public sector events.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Can we at least commit to, say, we will eliminate this by 2030?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: So, maybe not NDP 2019, but NDP 2030?
